transcript.text:
Thank you all for your formal status reports. Let me summarize what I'm recording for the approval decision:

First, from product-safety counsel, Daniel Cho: Your completed finding is that the HomeGuard Mini condition meets the substantial-product-hazard standard under applicable CPSC guidance. Your function recommends that the filing report an immediate consumer recall rather than continued monitoring. I note your full analysis is still undergoing citation review and hasn't been circulated yet.

Second, from engineering, Maya Singh: Your completed finding is that exactly 3,840 units from production lot HG-24B are affected, and the malfunction was not found in other lots. Your function recommends scoping the product to lot HG-24B specifically. I note the reconciliation hasn't been uploaded to the shared system yet, pending source record attachment.

Third, from commercial-contracts counsel, Thomas Reed: Your completed finding is that each affected retailer must receive a written stop-sale notice, and the contractual consumer remedy is a replacement unit, not a refund. Your function recommends including written stop-sale notices and specifying replacement units as the consumer remedy. I note the contract matrix hasn't been circulated yet, pending retailer contact list confirmation.

Based on these three formal status reports, here is what I am recording as my approval decision:

- The CPSC action will be an immediate consumer recall, consistent with the substantial-product-hazard finding from product-safety counsel.
- The affected lot scope is production lot HG-24B, with an affected unit count of 3,840, per engineering's completed reconciliation.
- Retailer stop-sale notices are required, per commercial-contracts counsel's finding.
- The consumer remedy will be replacement units, consistent with our contractual obligations as identified by commercial-contracts counsel.

The current draft describing the issue as 'under evaluation' must be revised to reflect these determinations before submission.

I am also recording the following commitments as conditions of my approval: Daniel, your full legal analysis must complete citation review and be circulated before the final package is submitted. Maya, the reconciliation must be uploaded to the shared system with supporting source records before submission. Thomas, the contract matrix must be circulated once the retailer contact list is confirmed, and written stop-sale notices must be issued to all affected retailers.

Are there any objections to what I've recorded before I formalize this decision?
